substantive_reconstruction.translation_and_order: For fixed V define nu(A)=mu(A V^{-1}). Right multiplication is a measurable bijection; nu has mass one and nu(gA)=mu(g A V^{-1})=nu(A) by left invariance. Uniqueness of normalized left Haar on compact U(d) gives nu=mu. This proves the needed right invariance instead of calling a right substitution a left translation. Expanding the rotated argument groups U_N V_N=(UV)_N, with the adjoint in the reverse order. Set W=UV; then U=W V-dagger and U-dagger=V W-dagger. The outside factors consequently become V_M W_M-dagger and W_M V_M-dagger, respectively. The fixed V factors leave the integral, leaving exactly the original twirl of X. This proves covariance for arbitrary operators, not only invariant states. The original inverse-substitution gloss is not retained.
substantive_reconstruction.channel_and_schur_domain: Each integrand is T composed with two unitary conjugations. Every matrix amplification is positive and trace preservation holds pointwise; finite-dimensional integration preserves both, proving the averaged map CPTP. For positive-dimensional symmetric input set tau_N=Pi_N/q_d(N). It is invariant under every V_N. Covariance now implies Y=Tbar(tau_N) commutes with V_M. The compression Pi_M Y Pi_M acts on the irreducible symmetric U(d) representation, so Schur gives a scalar there. Taking its trace gives lambda/q_d(M), with lambda=tr(Pi_M Y) between zero and one. The conclusion is about one compressed output of one invariant input. It is not about every output or the whole superoperator. Off the symmetric sector, unitary commutation leaves End(V_lambda) tensor I on multiplicity factors, not generally a scalar. I checked the factor order against the actual Schur-Weyl decomposition rather than treating all isotypic blocks as irreducible.
substantive_reconstruction.counterexample_and_edges: For d2 and N=M1, T=identity is fixed by this twirl: U-dagger (U X U-dagger) U=X. At X=|0><0| its output is a rank-one projector rather than a scalar multiple of I on the two-dimensional symmetric space. This simultaneously disproves the old scalar-output gloss and shows why covariance is not ordinary endomorphism scalarity applied to a superoperator. Zero tensor powers are the one-dimensional tensor unit, so the same covariance calculation is valid for N0 or M0. For d1 all relevant nonzero blocks are one dimensional. If d0 and a positive tensor power has zero dimension, there is no trace-one tau on it; divisions by q_0(r) are not performed. The conditional phrase about existence of such a channel does not invent a trace-preserving map into a zero space from a nonzero input.
